messages:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — Elevated edge TLS handshake failures detected affecting API reachability in SFO/LAX Cloudflare POPs. Alert: edge.tls.handshake.failures > 5% across 10m window. PagerDuty: page sent to #oncall.

lee_oncall: seeing 5xx spike to our /v1/generate endpoints, started investigating. datadog graphs show spike at 12:00 UTC.

shreya_sre: confirmed. Datadog alert "edge.tls.handshake.failures" tied to Cloudflare edge. Sample from logs: ```
[2026-03-15T12:00:57Z] svc=api edge_pop=SFO tls_error="tls: handshake failure" remote_ip=198.51.100.23 path=/v1/generate status=0
```

mike_edl: customer reports: intermittent 502/524 on multiple clients in US-WEST. Slack thread from support: "lots of TLS timeouts, clients fall back but many fail."

matt_support: I'm compiling a customer-impact list now — internal ticket redwood/incident-18345. Initial estimate: ~12% of production requests in us-west impacted. Affected customers: a few enterprise integrations using strict TLS settings + some private dedicated endpoints.

claire_network: running quick check against Cloudflare status and our DNS: Cloudflare reports degraded performance in SFO region (https://www.cloudflarestatus.com/). I can reproduce handshake failures from our probe box in SFO: ```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health 
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (104.16.99.52) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: Alert (no available ciphers)
* Closing connection 0
```

lee_oncall: I'm toggling routing policy to prefer us-east region (hot route) to reduce impact while we triage. Applying temporary route override via console. Will watch latency and error rate.

shreya_sre: please attach the exact console action and config snippet for the audit log. Also enable additional logging on the TLS handshake failures (edge.trace_id + client_ip) so we can hand to CF.

lee_oncall: console change command (internal): ```
POST /routing/policies/active 
{ "policy": "prefer-region", "region": "us-east-1", "priority": 100, "note": "temp fallback for SFO/LAX Cloudflare TLS failures" }
```
Change pushed at 12:05 UTC. Rolling out 30s.

dave_engineering: I pushed a client-side retry header experiment to force `Connection: close` for affected routes (to avoid stuck TLS sessions). If we see improvements we can roll further.

mike_edl: after route change errors dropped from 12% -> 3% in 3 minutes. Good short-term mitigation. Still seeing a tail of TLS errors ~1-2%.

matt_support: posted initial status page update: "We are investigating reports of intermittent API errors for customers in US-West. We have applied routing mitigations to reduce impact. More updates shortly."

claire_network: request to CF support opened — include pcap and edge trace IDs. Packet capture from probe: ```
PCAP-ID: pcap-20260315-sfo-01
tcpdump -w /tmp/sfo_tls_fail.pcap host 104.16.99.52 and port 443
```
Also include sample trace IDs from our logs: trace=0x9f3a2b, trace=0x9f3a2c

shreya_sre: assign to CF escalation. Put priority P1 and reference our SLAs. Ask for cause: misconfigured cipher negotiation? edge kernel overload? Also ask about possible rollbacks at their edge.

incident_bot: On-call handoff reminder: lee_oncall -> shreya_sre at 12:15 UTC. Please acknowledge with `:white_check_mark:` when takeover complete.

lee_oncall: handing off to @shreya_sre. I've left routing override active and removed any destructive changes. Logs and actions documented in the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

shreya_sre: acknowledged. I'm taking over. Current state: route override active, errors down to 2.8%, continuing to collect CF responses.

mike_edl: customer update draft: "We've applied a temporary routing change to mitigate an edge TLS issue affecting US-West. Some clients may still observe transient errors; engineering is actively working with our CDN provider for a long-term fix." Thoughts?

matt_support: looks good. Add "no data breach" and "we will follow up with post-incident analysis and remediation timeline."

shreya_sre: received response from Cloudflare support: "Investigating anomalies in SFO POP affecting TLS handshakes. Root cause under review. Temporary mitigation: our side rolling traffic away from affected edge nodes. Monitoring." They asked for our sample traces and PCAP. Uploaded pcap and trace IDs.

claire_network: CF also asked for exact client hello bytes for a few failed handshakes — sent via secure upload. They asked whether we use strict TLS 1.3 ciphers — we do for enterprise endpoints (no TLS 1.2 fallback). That could explain why some clients fail.

dave_engineering: quick workaround idea: allow TLS 1.2 fallback for enterprise endpoints for the next 2 hours via config flag `allow_tls12_temp=true`. This reduces security posture slightly but could restore connectivity for strict clients. Need approval.

matt_support: I need decision ASAP — several paying customers impacted. Suggest enabling fallback only for known enterprise customer subnets, not globally.

shreya_sre: agree with restricted fallback. Claire, can you prepare the access list for enterprise subnets?

claire_network: done. List ready, pushing policy scoped to enterprise subnets now. Policy change: ```
PATCH /tls/policies/enterprise 
{ "allow_tls12_temp": true, "scope": "enterprise_subnets_marked" }
```
Applied at 12:42 UTC. Monitoring.

mike_edl: after scoped TLS fallback errors decreased another 0.8%. Enterprise customers reporting recovery. Good.

shreya_sre: CF updated: they removed affected nodes from rotation and are performing kernel-level restart on a subset of SFO hosts. They expect full resolution within 30–90 minutes. Asking us to keep routing override for safer ramp down.

matt_support: posted second customer update with ETA and mitigation notes.

lee_oncall: small note for postmortem: we saw correlation with a Cloudflare kernel patch rolling at 11:55 UTC — CF noted earlier scheduled deploys but said this looked unrelated. Save that for RCA.

incident_bot: Paging: primary on-call incident window ends at 13:00 UTC, active handover in progress.

shreya_sre: I'll keep monitoring and coordinate final rollback. Action items: 1) Collect final CF support logs and confirm cause, 2) Schedule postmortem with network, infra, and support, 3) Rollback routing override only when CF confirms stable, 4) Revert scoped TLS fallback once confirmed safe.

matt_support: creating the incident page and PM template now. Will include impacted customer list and timeline.

claire_network: CF just posted fix status: SFO POPs stable, TLS handshake failure metrics back to baseline. I see handshake failure metric below threshold for 10m. Recommend ramp-down of override after 10m stable.

shreya_sre: starting ramp-down of prefer-region override at 13:04 UTC — will step down in 2 minutes and monitor for 15m.

dave_engineering: rolling back `allow_tls12_temp` for enterprise subnets now.

mike_edl: monitoring shows no regression after rollback. Error rate remains <0.5%.

matt_support: final status update posted: "Issue resolved — Cloudflare SFO POP TLS handshake failures caused intermittent API errors. We applied routing and TLS scope mitigations. No data lost. Postmortem forthcoming."

shreya_sre: handing incident to follow-up queue. Thanks everyone for the quick coordination. :heart:

incident_bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — root channel will be archived.
